headline: Suspected Binance hack drags bitcoin down 4.9 percent as Alphabet's earnings miss hits tech
subhead: Ether fell 6.1 percent, the Nasdaq lost 1.4 percent and the S&P 500 0.3 percent after Alphabet missed estimates, while the US 10 year yield eased 1.1 percent to 4.99 percent.

us.text: Nasdaq fell 1.4 percent to 26,185 and the S&P 500 0.3 percent to 7,720 as Alphabet sank on an earnings miss driven by an 8.7 billion dollar investment loss.
Third quarter GDP grew 3.4 percent annualised against 3.1 expected, and core PCE inflation held at 3.1 percent, keeping December hike bets alive.
Amazon slid after hours on negative free cash flow of 42.4 billion dollars and fourth quarter guidance below consensus; Apple reports on 2 November.

india.text: Nifty 50 rebounded to 22,936.75 and the Sensex to 74,151.04 on 29 October on the Fed hold and hopes of a long-term capital gains tax cut.
FIIs were net sellers of 943.60 crore rupees in cash on 29 October while DIIs bought a net 1,924.41 crore.
The rupee settled at 95.25 per dollar (provisional), up 3 paise, helped by firmer equities and softer crude oil.

global.text: KOSPI fell 4.7 percent in Friday trade after Thursday's drop, when Samsung's shareholder return plan disappointed despite record profit; the Bank of Japan decides today.
The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50 percent and flagged energy-driven inflation risk; the DAX closed at 26,052.75.
Gold fell 0.7 percent to 4,023 dollars and silver 2.8 percent as strong US growth and inflation data supported Fed tightening bets.

weekly.narrative: Two forces ran the week and both pointed at the cost of capital. Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, including Iranian claims that seven vessels were hit or mined, took Brent above 117 dollars and WTI past 100, and because that lands as an inflation shock rather than a growth scare it lifted rate expectations instead of safe havens: gold closed the week below 4,000 dollars and now sits 1.6 percent above its 52 week low and silver hit a year to date low, while the US 10 year held near 4.99 percent. The second force was the AI financing question, which moved from equity multiples to credit, with a Lam Research warning on chip supply into 2027 knocking the Nasdaq 2.6 percent on Thursday, CoreWeave 2032 bonds quoted near 78 cents on the dollar, and Jensen Huang arguing the sector is short of capital rather than demand. India inverted the pattern, with the Nifty pressured by the oil bill and foreign selling while IT rallied on a reverse AI trade that reads weaker AI capex as work returning to traditional services firms, and the rupee closed at 94.93 against the dollar. Next week stacks the catalysts: the Fed decision on 28 October with a hike priced near 7.6 percent, Microsoft and Alphabet that same evening, Amazon plus Q3 GDP and September PCE on 29 October, the Bank of Japan on 30 October, and in Mumbai the listing of the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms issue alongside five new mainboard IPOs.
